corrections.new: India and the United States functioned as estranged democracies in opposing camps during the Cold War.
corrections.reason: Dennis Kux coined 'estranged democracies' for their Cold War estrangement; calling India an 'indispensable partner' was said by Ashton Carter.

quiz.q: Why is the 2005 Indo-US Civil Nuclear Agreement considered a major geopolitical breakthrough for India?
options: It compelled the United States to sign the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty alongside India.
It exempted India from placing any of its civilian nuclear facilities under IAEA safeguards.
It recognized India as a de-facto nuclear weapon state without requiring it to sign the NPT.
It allowed India to transfer uranium enrichment technology directly to non-aligned developing nations.
quiz.why: The agreement integrated India into global nuclear commerce and recognized it as a de-facto nuclear power without signing the NPT or CTBT.

quiz.q: Why did American nuclear reactor suppliers strongly object to Section 17(B) of India's nuclear liability law?
options: It allowed the operator to seek financial recourse from suppliers for equipment defects without contractual clauses.
It imposed strict criminal penalties solely on the operator while fully exempting all equipment suppliers.
It required American companies to pay compensation exclusively in Special Drawing Rights above the government cap.
It mandated that foreign suppliers manage the domestic insurance pool created by the Indian government.
quiz.why: Section 17(B) gives the operator the right of recourse against suppliers for defective equipment even without an explicit contractual clause.

quiz.q: How does India's 2015 Model Bilateral Investment Treaty differ fundamentally from the 2012 United States model?
options: India adopts an asset-based approach protecting financial derivatives, while the United States demands an enterprise-based approach.
India grants automatic Most Favoured Nation treatment, while the United States insists on case-by-case bilateral negotiations.
India mandates immediate international arbitration, whereas the United States requires exhausting all local court remedies first.
India requires substantial physical presence and local employment, whereas the United States model protects diverse financial assets.
quiz.why: India's model is enterprise-based requiring physical presence and employment, whereas the US model is asset-based protecting shares, derivatives, and intellectual property.

quiz.q: Under Section 84 of the Indian Patents Act, when can the government issue a compulsory licence for a medicine?
options: Immediately upon patent grant whenever a foreign pharmaceutical manufacturer begins commercial production in India.
After three years if the drug is unaffordable, unavailable commercially, or needed for public health.
Only after the original 20-year patent term has fully expired without any increase in therapeutic efficacy.
Whenever an international arbitration tribunal directs India to suspend patent rights under TRIPS flexibilities.
quiz.why: Section 84 permits compulsory licensing after three years if the medicine is overpriced, not commercially worked in India, or needed for public health.
